body:
Parent: #245 (the mounted route is the product surface). Related: #249 (command lease and the whole-Exec timer), #70 (FUSE request count and local callback cost), #69 (durability and fsync semantics — **not** this issue), #256 (the 1,024-entry cookie table), #258 (base-resident directory `mv` refusal).

Source pin: `7a81213ba` (lane head `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation`). Line links are to that commit; the FUSE crate is unchanged by the in-flight 3.4 work.

## The mount surface is closed and mostly good practice — these are the gaps in it

The adapter negotiates a tight, fail-closed envelope: `init` sets `max_write`/`max_readahead` = 128 KiB, `max_background = 1`, `congestion_threshold = 1`, and returns an error if any of them cannot be set ([adapter.rs:113](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L113)); every regular open uses `FOPEN_DIRECT_IO`; the mount options are `RO`/`RW`, `NoSuid`, `NoDev`, `DefaultPermissions`, `Exec`, `NoAtime`, `max_read=131072` with `SessionACL::Owner` and two session threads ([mount.rs:208](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/mount.rs#L208)). Unimplemented operations answer `EOPNOTSUPP`/`ENOSYS`, never a silent success. Three things are nevertheless open, and one of them is user-visible in any interactive shell.

## Gap 1 — an in-flight callback cannot be cancelled (no interrupt handling)

- The adapter handles no `FUSE_INTERRUPT`: there is no `interrupted` reference in `layerfs-fuse`, and `fuser` 0.18 (the pinned version) exposes **no** `Filesystem::interrupt` method at all, so the workspace is never told that a caller was interrupted.
- The only bound on a started callback is `CALLBACK_BUDGET = 10 s` ([adapter.rs:21](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L21)), which the mount documents as "deadline observation points, not preemption" ([mount.rs:136](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/mount.rs#L136)).
- Consequence to be **measured, not assumed**: what a caller sees when it interrupts a blocked callback (e.g. Ctrl-C on a slow `ls`/`cp`), and whether the interrupted mutation is still published afterwards. A mutation that lands after its caller was told the operation was interrupted is a correctness question for the product contract, not only a latency question.

What a fix requires: cancellation, not a bigger timeout. Because third-party crates may not be patched or vendored, the legitimate routes are (a) own the low-level session reader in-crate instead of relying on `fuser`'s dispatch, or (b) record the bounded-step behaviour as the accepted contract with its exact observable shape. This issue is for deciding that with evidence; it is not a licence to raise `CALLBACK_BUDGET` or to special-case a command.

## Gap 2 — no crash-safe unmount

- No `MountOption::AutoUnmount` is requested, and the mount is owned by a session thread inside the daemon ([mount.rs:230](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/mount.rs#L230)).
- If that process is killed hard (`kill -9`, OOM kill, container stop), the mount is left with no server: users of the mount point can block in the kernel until someone unmounts it by hand. Every FUSE filesystem has this hazard; here it is unstated and untested.
- Expected: an explicit statement of what a dead daemon leaves behind and how it is recovered (unmount command, lease/`reserve_mount` behaviour, whether a later attach can reclaim the path), or `AutoUnmount` plus a test that death is observed. Custody of unknown Commit outcomes is a different layer and is already covered by the Workspace contract.

## Gap 3 — `statfs` reports zeros

- `statfs` answers `reply.statfs(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4096, 255, 4096)` ([adapter.rs:400](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L400)) — block size and name length are real, the totals and free counts are zero.
- Consequence: `df` shows an empty filesystem, and any tool that checks free space before writing (package installers, `rsync --preallocate`, some build systems) may refuse for the wrong reason or misreport capacity. The Workspace already carries a configured `disk_budget_bytes`, so a truthful figure exists to report.
- Expected: report the declared budget (or document why zeros are the contract and what tools must not infer from them).

## What is deliberate and must not be "fixed"

Recording these so a later agent does not undo them: direct I/O on every open (no page-cache coherence problem), `max_background = 1` (bounded, chargeable steps), `TTL = ZERO` ([adapter.rs:22](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L22)), `fsync`/`fsyncdir` → `EOPNOTSUPP` ([adapter.rs:407](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L407)), `getxattr`/`listxattr`/`readdirplus` → `EOPNOTSUPP`, `setxattr`/`removexattr` → `EOPNOTSUPP` on a writable mount and `EROFS` on a read-only one ([adapter.rs:69](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L69)), `RENAME_EXCHANGE`/`RENAME_WHITEOUT` → `EINVAL`, a single write over 128 KiB → `E2BIG` ([adapter.rs:539](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L539)), regular files only in `mknod`. Each is a declared boundary with continuation or an explicit refusal; none is a bug.

## Acceptance

1. **Interrupt case.** With a callback deliberately held (a slow operation on the mounted tree), signal the caller and record exactly: the syscall's return, whether the callback completed, whether the mutation was published, and the elapsed time. Then state the contract: cancellation, or a bounded step with the observable shape documented. Repeat for a read, a write and a rename, since the three take different paths. Report `EINTR`/timeout outcomes and the published state; do not claim "interrupt works" from one path.
2. **Daemon-death case.** Kill the serving process while a mount is live; record what a subsequent `stat`, `ls` and `df` on the mount point do, how long they block, and the exact recovery command. If the answer is `AutoUnmount`, assert the mount point is gone within a bounded time and that a later attach can reclaim the path.
3. **`statfs` case.** Compare `df` and `statvfs` output against the configured `disk_budget_bytes`, for an empty workspace and after writes, and assert the numbers are truthful or that the zeros are documented with the tool consequences.
4. **Refusal table case.** One mounted case per refused operation asserting the documented errno (`fsync`, `getxattr`, `setxattr`, oversize write, `RENAME_EXCHANGE`, `mknod` of a FIFO), so the envelope cannot drift into a silent success. The FUSE callbacks are exercised today only below the mount, so this needs a real mount: use the recorded container recipe (`rust:1.85.1-bookworm`, `layerfs-i245-phase1`) or an equivalent Linux ext4 volume.

No performance or POSIX-conformance claim is made or implied by this issue. A conformance run (`pjdfstest`/LTP/`fsx` — currently referenced only inside the peer study under `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/study/drive9/`) and a crash/`kill -9` stress case would each need their own issue; `fsync` durability semantics stay with #69, FUSE request counts with #70, the base-resident directory `mv` refusal with #258, and the listing cookie table with #256.
title: FUSE mount surface: callback interruption, crash-safe unmount and a zeroed statfs
